exit: after repeated verification, Nari observes a reproducible correspondence between the anomaly and the forbidden lower temple and chooses to investigate despite fear

title: Beneath the God-Stone
purpose: Scene 2 rewards and punishes Nari’s curiosity: she discovers repeatable correspondences that show the inherited model is incomplete, while the scale and strangeness of what she encounters deepen her fear and deny her a replacement explanation.
setting: upper temple service ways and forbidden lower temple beneath the God-Stone after the failed High Count
entry: Nari follows the verified lower-temple correspondence in secret, curious enough to proceed but increasingly afraid of what confirmation may mean
exit: Nari has established that the lower chamber, God-Stone, and sky anomaly participate in the same repeatable pattern, but she understands the phenomenon less rather than more; Orem calls from above as the chamber responds in a way she cannot explain
required_movements: Nari remains after the failed High Count and chooses inquiry over obedience while acknowledging her fear

title: The Answering Light
purpose: Scene 3 confronts curiosity with fear without declaring either sufficient. Fear can protect by restricting exposure but also restrict knowledge; curiosity can expand knowledge but also reveal things whose consequences may exceed human understanding. Orem and Nari each glimpse the cost of their own extreme without reaching the balance between them.
setting: lower temple chamber beneath the God-Stone, continuing directly from Scene 2
entry: Nari stands in the responding lower chamber with stronger evidence, growing fear, and no adequate explanation as Orem arrives
exit: the answering light comes after Nari permits the observed pattern to continue; Orem is left with remorse over knowledge fear may have kept from him, Nari understands that curiosity can uncover things safer left unknown, and neither reaches a stable balance between curiosity and fear
